stem: In the Now Platform, where are user records stored?

options.text: On the sys_user table.
On the sys_user_group table.
On the sys_user_role table.
On the sys_user_has_role table.

rationale: User records live on the sys_user table. The other user-administration tables (groups, roles, role assignments) all reference back to sys_user for the individual user.

distractor_notes.B: sys_user_group holds the groups themselves (one row per group), not individual users.
distractor_notes.C: sys_user_role is the catalog of roles available in the instance, not where users live.
distractor_notes.D: sys_user_has_role is the join table that links users to roles — useful, but it doesn't store the user records.

stem: Which statement best describes a group in ServiceNow?

options.text: A collection of users that can be assigned roles, used as approvers.
A reusable security ACL applied to specific tables.
A view of users filtered by department.
A role variant scoped to one application.

rationale: A group is a collection of users (records on sys_user_group). Groups can carry roles that flow to their members, be used as approvers, and be assignment targets on tasks — that's why they're the workhorse for assignment routing.

distractor_notes.B: ACLs are access control rules. They can require roles, but groups themselves aren't ACLs.
distractor_notes.C: Department is a separate field on the user record. A group isn't just a department filter.
distractor_notes.D: Roles can be application-scoped, but a group isn't a 'scoped role'. Groups carry roles; they aren't roles.

stem: How are roles typically granted to a user in ServiceNow?

options.text: Directly on the user record, indirectly through group membership.
Only by editing the sys_user_has_role table with a SQL update.
Only by being a member of an organization unit.
Only by activating a plugin that ships the role.

rationale: Roles can be granted directly on the user, granted to a group the user belongs to (the user inherits the group's roles), or contained by another role (parent roles include their child roles). All three paths produce effective permissions.

distractor_notes.B: You don't run SQL to assign roles — you use the platform UI. sys_user_has_role is the join table behind the scenes.
distractor_notes.C: Org unit / department doesn't grant roles by itself.
distractor_notes.D: Plugins can ship new roles, but activating a plugin doesn't assign those roles to users automatically.

references.title: Assign a role to a user

stem: An admin needs every member of the "ServiceDesk" group to be able to read incidents. What is the most maintainable way to grant that access?

options.text: Assign the appropriate role to the ServiceDesk group.
Manually add the role to every user one at a time on sys_user.
Edit the incident table ACL to bypass role checks for ServiceDesk.
Make every user a system administrator.

rationale: Assigning the role to the group is the maintainable pattern: every current and future member inherits the role just by being in the group. Removing someone from the group automatically removes the inherited access.

distractor_notes.B: Per-user assignment works once, but it drifts the moment the team changes — exactly what the group-based model is designed to avoid.
distractor_notes.C: Bypassing ACLs for one group is a security anti-pattern and isn't how role evaluation is supposed to work.
distractor_notes.D: Granting admin to everyone solves the access problem by destroying the security model. Don't.

references.title: Assign a role to a group

stem: Which role grants full administrative access to the Now Platform's core configuration and security?

options.text: itil
admin
approver_user
snc_internal

rationale: The admin role is the platform's super-role — it inherits and contains a large set of administrative roles and is required to perform broad configuration and security work.

distractor_notes.A: itil is the standard role for ITSM agents (incidents, problems, changes). It is not a platform admin.
distractor_notes.C: approver_user lets a user act on approval requests assigned to them. It grants no admin power.
distractor_notes.D: snc_internal is for ServiceNow-internal/HI integrations. It is not the platform admin role.

stem: A developer needs to verify how the Service Catalog appears to an end user with no ITIL role. Which administrative tool is designed for this?

options.text: Impersonate User
Update Set Preview
Performance Analytics
System Log Replay

rationale: Impersonate User lets an admin temporarily browse the platform as another user. It's the supported way to verify what someone with a different role profile actually sees, and the platform logs every impersonation for accountability.

distractor_notes.B: Update Set Preview compares incoming changes to the target instance. It has nothing to do with viewing the UI as another user.
distractor_notes.C: Performance Analytics is a reporting and KPI tool. It does not switch your view to another user's perspective.
distractor_notes.D: 'System Log Replay' is not a standard platform tool. You can't replay another user's session this way.

stem: Which statement most accurately describes plugins in the Now Platform?

options.text: Bundles of platform features and content that an administrator activates on the instance to enable additional functionality.
Browser extensions installed in the user's browser.
Third-party Node packages installed through npm.
External services connected by REST that run outside the instance.

rationale: Plugins package platform features (tables, scripts, UI, demo data, roles, etc.) that an admin activates on an instance. Activation enables the functionality and, where applicable, loads demo data.

distractor_notes.B: Plugins live in the instance, not in the browser. They aren't browser extensions.
distractor_notes.C: Plugins are not npm packages. ServiceNow has its own packaging model.
distractor_notes.D: External services connected by REST are integrations, not plugins. Plugins run inside the instance.

stem: An administrator activates a plugin on a sub-production instance and chooses to load demo data. Which statement is true?

options.text: The demo data is for evaluation only and is typically not loaded on production instances.
Demo data is encrypted and cannot be deleted after activation.
Demo data is added to the current update set automatically.
Demo data overwrites any existing records of the same table.

rationale: Demo data is intended to help admins and developers evaluate a plugin in a sub-production environment. It's standard practice not to load demo data on a production instance.

distractor_notes.B: Demo data is regular platform data — it isn't encrypted, and it can be removed.
distractor_notes.C: Plugin activation and the demo data it ships are tracked separately from a developer's current update set.
distractor_notes.D: Demo data is inserted; it doesn't overwrite existing records of the same table based on field collisions.

stem: What is the primary purpose of application scope in the Now Platform?

options.text: It identifies and protects the resources.
It defines which physical data center hosts the application.
It controls which time zone the application runs in.
It limits how many users may use the application concurrently.

rationale: Application scope namespaces an application's resources and governs cross-scope access. It's how the platform keeps applications from stepping on each other and lets app developers expose only what they intend to share.

distractor_notes.B: Application scope is a logical construct. It has nothing to do with data center placement.
distractor_notes.C: Time zone is a system / user setting, not a scope concept.
distractor_notes.D: User concurrency is a licensing and capacity matter, not what scope governs.

stem: Which statement best describes an update set?

options.text: A group of customizations that can be moved from one instance to another.
A snapshot of every record in the database.
A backup of the instance's binary attachments only.
A scheduled job that runs nightly to clean log tables.

rationale: An update set is a portable container for configuration changes (the things admins and developers customize — UI, scripts, policies, etc.) that can be exported from one instance and applied to another.

distractor_notes.B: Update sets don't capture data records. They capture configuration changes tracked by the platform.
distractor_notes.C: Update sets are for configuration, not for attachments or binaries.
distractor_notes.D: Update sets are not scheduled jobs. They're an artifact you move between instances.

stem: A developer is about to make a series of configuration changes on a development instance that they will later promote to test and production. What should they do first?

options.text: Create and select a new, named update set as the current update set on the dev instance.
Disable system logging so the changes are not captured.
Activate the demo-data plugin so the changes capture sample records.
Switch the dev instance into Read-Only mode.

rationale: Before making changes meant for promotion, create a new update set and set it as your current set. Every captured change then lands in that named update set, which you can later export and apply to test and production.

distractor_notes.B: Disabling logging would just blind the admin. Update sets track configuration changes regardless.
distractor_notes.C: Demo data is for evaluation; it isn't a promotion mechanism.
distractor_notes.D: Read-Only mode prevents changes — exactly the opposite of what's needed.

references.title: Create and select an update set as the current set

stem: An admin wants to view and edit the platform's system properties in one place. Which list path do they enter in the Application Navigator filter?

options.text: sys_properties.list
sys_user.list
sys_dictionary.list
syslog.list

rationale: System properties live on the sys_properties table. Entering sys_properties.list in the filter opens the full list — the standard way for an admin to view, search, and edit platform configuration values.

distractor_notes.B: sys_user.list opens the users table, not the system properties.
distractor_notes.C: sys_dictionary.list shows the data dictionary (field metadata), not configuration properties.
distractor_notes.D: syslog.list shows the system log. It's diagnostic output, not configuration.

stem: Which statement best describes a notification in the Now Platform?

options.text: A record on a table that defines when and to whom the platform sends an email, SMS.
A toast popup that always appears at the top of the form when a record is saved.
An audit log entry of a field change on a record.
A scheduled job that runs every hour to clean the syslog table.

rationale: Notifications are configuration records that tell the platform when to send a message (email, SMS, push), to whom, and with what content. They can be triggered by record events or by record conditions on insert/update.

distractor_notes.B: Toast popups are UI feedback. They're unrelated to the notifications subsystem.
distractor_notes.C: Audit log entries are read-only history. They don't drive notifications by themselves.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduled cleanup jobs maintain log tables. They aren't the notifications feature.

stem: An admin needs to send an email to the assignee whenever an incident's priority is set to 1 - Critical. Which configuration accomplishes this most directly?

options.text: Create an email notification on the Incident table with a condition that priority equals 1 and 'When to send' set to send on record update.
Add a UI policy that hides the priority field for non-admins.
Create an ACL that denies write access to incidents with priority 1.
Write a client script that calls window.alert when priority changes.

rationale: The right tool is an email notification on the Incident table — set the condition to priority = 1, the trigger to record update, and the To/recipients to the assigned_to field. That's exactly the use case notifications are designed for.

distractor_notes.B: UI policies change form visibility/behavior. They don't send email.
distractor_notes.C: ACLs control access, not communications.
distractor_notes.D: window.alert is a browser popup for the current user. Notifications need to reach the assignee even when they're not on the form.

stem: What is the role of email properties (the email-related system properties) on an instance?

options.text: They control instance-level email behavior such as sending enable/disable, test mode, SMTP/IMAP configuration values.
They store the personal email signature for every user.
They cache outbound email attachments for performance.
They define the user's preferred font for the inbox UI.

rationale: Email properties are the instance-level switches that control how the platform sends and receives email — enable/disable sending, test mode, mail server configuration, and how inbound replies are interpreted.

distractor_notes.B: Personal signatures are user-level settings, not instance email properties.
distractor_notes.C: Attachment caching isn't what email properties are for.
distractor_notes.D: Inbox UI fonts are unrelated to email properties.

stem: Before exporting an update set from a source instance, what state should it normally be set to?

options.text: In Progress
Complete
Ignored
Build

rationale: Setting an update set to Complete signals that you're done making changes inside it and that it's ready to be picked up by a target instance. In Progress sets aren't intended for promotion.

distractor_notes.A: In Progress means you're still capturing changes. Promote a Complete set, not an in-progress one.
distractor_notes.C: Ignored update sets aren't promoted at all.
distractor_notes.D: There is no 'Build' state in the update set lifecycle.

stem: On the target (test or production) instance, what is the typical order for applying an update set received from another instance?

options.text: Retrieve → Preview → Commit
Commit → Retrieve → Preview
Preview → Commit → Retrieve
Export → Import → Validate

rationale: On the target instance you Retrieve the remote update set (pull it across), Preview it (resolve any collisions or warnings), and then Commit it (apply the changes to the instance). Doing those steps out of order is the classic foot-gun.

distractor_notes.B: Committing before retrieving is impossible — there's nothing to commit yet.
distractor_notes.C: Preview comes after Retrieve, not first.
distractor_notes.D: Export/Import/Validate isn't the supported update-set vocabulary.

stem: During preview, the target instance reports an update set collision. What is the correct response?

options.text: Investigate the collision, choose to accept remote, skip.
Force-commit without resolving — collisions are informational only.
Delete the target record manually, then re-preview.
Restart the instance to clear the collision cache.

rationale: Collisions surface during preview so the admin can decide what to do per change — accept the incoming change, skip it, or merge — before committing. That deliberation is the whole point of the preview step.

distractor_notes.B: Commits don't ignore unresolved problems quietly. The preview step exists so problems are addressed first.
distractor_notes.C: Deleting target records by hand is dangerous and not the supported workflow for collision resolution.
distractor_notes.D: Restarting doesn't change the underlying conflict; the data is still incompatible.

stem: Which type of change is NOT captured in a standard update set?

options.text: A new business rule script.
A new UI policy.
A new incident record submitted by an end user.
A new client script.

rationale: Update sets capture configuration changes — scripts, policies, forms, fields, and so on. Operational data records (an incident the team logged today) are not configuration and aren't carried in update sets.

distractor_notes.A: Business rules are configuration — they are captured.
distractor_notes.B: UI policies are configuration — they are captured.
distractor_notes.D: Client scripts are configuration — they are captured.

stem: Where does an administrator change the company logo that appears in the Next Experience global header?

options.text: Through the platform's branding/Next Experience configuration that updates the instance logo.
By renaming the favicon.svg in the OS file system.
By writing a script include named CompanyLogo.
By editing the user's profile picture.

rationale: The instance logo for the Next Experience header is changed through the platform's branding configuration — the supported, upgrade-safe path. It updates centrally and applies for all users.

distractor_notes.B: Instances aren't browsed as files; you can't rename favicon assets on a host file system.
distractor_notes.C: Script includes are reusable server scripts. They aren't where you set the logo.
distractor_notes.D: A user's profile picture is just their avatar — not the company branding.

references.title: Change instance banner logo in Next Experience

stem: Which statement is true about a custom scoped application?

options.text: Its resources are namespaced and the application controls how other scopes may read or write them.
It is automatically global — all scopes have full access by default.
It cannot have its own update sets.
It cannot define new roles.

rationale: Scoped apps namespace their resources and use explicit access settings to govern what other scopes can do with them. That isolation is what makes scope a useful packaging boundary.

distractor_notes.B: Scoped apps are not global. Cross-scope access is opt-in.
distractor_notes.C: Scoped apps absolutely have their own update tracking.
distractor_notes.D: Scoped apps can define their own roles.

stem: An admin wants to start a new custom application on their developer instance. Which tool is the supported starting point?

options.text: Studio (the application development workspace).
The CMDB Health dashboard.
A Service Portal page builder widget.
Performance Analytics.

rationale: Studio is the application development environment for creating and managing custom applications, their files, and source control. It's the supported entry point for new custom apps.

distractor_notes.B: The CMDB Health dashboard is for CMDB data quality. It doesn't create applications.
distractor_notes.C: Service Portal page builder builds portal pages, not applications.
distractor_notes.D: Performance Analytics is analytics tooling, not an app dev environment.

stem: A developer makes a change while the global Default update set is selected. Where does that change land?

options.text: In the Default update set.
In the most recently committed update set on production.
In a temporary in-memory buffer that disappears on logout.
In all open update sets simultaneously.

rationale: The Default update set is a catch-all for changes made when no purposeful set is active. It captures the change but is not the right vehicle for moving deliberate work between instances — always select a named set before making changes you intend to promote.

distractor_notes.B: Production update sets aren't auto-edited by other instances. There's no remote write.
distractor_notes.C: Changes persist; they aren't held in memory only.
distractor_notes.D: There is exactly one current update set at a time per scope.

stem: A change committed via update set unexpectedly broke a related list on production. What is the most appropriate immediate response?

options.text: Use the Back Out option on the committed update set to reverse the captured changes, then investigate.
Disable the entire instance until next maintenance window.
Delete the affected related list manually so users don't see it.
Re-import the same update set a second time.

rationale: Committed update sets can be backed out, which reverses the changes they applied. It's the right first move when a commit causes a regression — restore the prior state, then root-cause the problem on a sub-prod instance.

distractor_notes.B: Disabling the instance is wildly disproportionate and isn't a normal recovery step.
distractor_notes.C: Manual deletes create more drift and don't address the root cause.
distractor_notes.D: Re-importing the same broken change doesn't help.

stem: Which field on the sys_user record, when set to true, marks a user as a VIP and can affect notification behavior?

options.text: active
vip
priority_user
elevated

rationale: The vip boolean field on the sys_user record marks a user as a VIP. This field can be used in notification conditions and business rules to apply special handling.

distractor_notes.A: The active field controls whether the user account is enabled or disabled, not VIP status.
distractor_notes.C: priority_user is not a standard sys_user field.
distractor_notes.D: elevated is not a standard sys_user field.

stem: What is the effect of setting a user's 'active' field to false on their sys_user record?

options.text: The user's records are deleted from the instance
The user can no longer log into the instance
The user's role assignments are permanently removed
The user is moved to an archived user table

rationale: Setting active to false on a sys_user record disables the account, preventing the user from logging in. Their data and records remain intact.

distractor_notes.A: Records are not deleted when a user is deactivated.
distractor_notes.C: Role assignments are retained when a user is deactivated; they take effect again if the user is reactivated.
distractor_notes.D: There is no archived user table in the standard platform.

stem: What is the table name for user records in ServiceNow?

options.text: sys_user_group
sys_user
sys_person
user_profile

rationale: User records in ServiceNow are stored in the sys_user table. Each row represents one authenticated user account.

distractor_notes.A: sys_user_group stores group records, not individual user records.
distractor_notes.C: sys_person is not a standard ServiceNow table.
distractor_notes.D: user_profile is not the standard table for user accounts.

stem: Which table stores group records in ServiceNow?

options.text: sys_user
sys_group
sys_user_group
sys_team

rationale: Group records in ServiceNow are stored in the sys_user_group table. Groups are used for assignments, notifications, and role grants.

distractor_notes.A: sys_user stores individual user records.
distractor_notes.B: sys_group is not a standard ServiceNow table name.
distractor_notes.D: sys_team is not the standard table for groups.

stem: An admin needs to ensure all members of the 'Network' group inherit the network_admin role. What is the most efficient approach?

options.text: Assign the network_admin role directly to each user in the group
Assign the network_admin role to the Network group so all members inherit it
Create a scheduled job that assigns the role nightly
Use an ACL to restrict access based on group membership

rationale: Assigning a role to a group grants that role to all current and future members of the group. This is the most efficient way to manage role inheritance for a set of users.

distractor_notes.A: Assigning roles individually to each user is inefficient and requires manual updates as membership changes.
distractor_notes.C: A scheduled job is unnecessary when role inheritance via group assignment handles this automatically.
distractor_notes.D: ACLs control access to records, not role assignments.

stem: Which field on a sys_user_group record designates the person responsible for managing the group?

options.text: owner
manager
group_lead
supervisor

rationale: The manager field on a sys_user_group record identifies the person responsible for managing the group.

distractor_notes.A: owner is not the standard field for group management in sys_user_group.
distractor_notes.C: group_lead is not a standard sys_user_group field.
distractor_notes.D: supervisor is not a standard sys_user_group field.

stem: Which role in ServiceNow contains all other roles and grants complete administrative access?

options.text: itil
admin
security_admin
superuser

rationale: The admin role in ServiceNow grants full administrative access to the core platform configuration. It contains all other roles implicitly.

distractor_notes.A: itil grants access to ITSM process modules but is a limited operational role, not a superadmin role.
distractor_notes.C: security_admin is a specialized role for security administration, not a full admin role.
distractor_notes.D: superuser is not a standard ServiceNow role.

stem: A scoped application defines a role called x_acme_app.approver. A user must have this role to approve records in the app. How is this role typically granted?

options.text: It is automatically granted to all admin users
It must be assigned directly to users or groups through the Roles related list
It is inherited from the itil role automatically
It is activated when the plugin for the scoped app is installed

rationale: Application-specific roles defined in a scoped app (like x_acme_app.approver) must be explicitly assigned to users or groups through the Roles related list on the user or group record.

distractor_notes.A: Admin does not automatically inherit application-specific scoped roles unless explicitly configured.
distractor_notes.C: itil is an ITSM role unrelated to custom scoped application roles.
distractor_notes.D: Plugin installation activates features but does not auto-grant scoped roles to users.

stem: What is the effect of a role containing another role in ServiceNow?

options.text: The child role is deprecated when the parent role is assigned
Users with the parent role automatically have the permissions of all contained roles
The contained role must also be assigned separately to take effect
Contained roles only apply in global scope

rationale: When a role contains another role, users assigned the parent role automatically receive all permissions granted by the contained (child) roles. This is how role inheritance works in ServiceNow.

distractor_notes.A: Contained roles are not deprecated; they are inherited.
distractor_notes.C: Contained roles do not need to be separately assigned; the parent role grants them automatically.
distractor_notes.D: Role containment works across scopes, not just global scope.

stem: Before activating a plugin, what should an administrator verify first?

options.text: That the plugin is listed in the ServiceNow Store
That the plugin has not already been activated on the instance
That all existing update sets have been committed
That the instance is running the latest release

rationale: Before requesting or activating a plugin, admins should check whether the plugin has already been activated on the instance to avoid duplicate activation attempts.

distractor_notes.A: Not all plugins are in the Store; some are available through the Application Manager regardless.
distractor_notes.C: Committing update sets is a pre-deployment best practice but is not the first verification step for plugin activation.
distractor_notes.D: Plugin activation is not restricted to the latest release.

stem: Where does an administrator navigate to activate a plugin in ServiceNow?

options.text: System Properties > Plugins
All > System Applications > All Available Applications > All
All > System Definition > Plugins
Admin Center > Plugins

rationale: To activate a plugin, navigate to All > System Applications > All Available Applications > All, then find the plugin using filter criteria or search and select Install.

distractor_notes.A: System Properties is for configuration settings, not plugin activation.
distractor_notes.C: All > System Definition > Plugins is an older navigation path; the current path is through System Applications.
distractor_notes.D: Admin Center is a configuration hub, not where plugins are activated.

stem: When domain separation and delegated admin are enabled, what domain must the activating admin be in to avoid a plugin activation error?

options.text: The top-level domain of the organization
The global domain
The admin's home domain
Any domain with the plugin_admin role

rationale: When domain separation and delegated admin are enabled, the administrative user activating a plugin must be in the global domain. Otherwise, an error appears indicating another operation is running.

distractor_notes.A: The top-level organizational domain is not the same as the global domain in domain separation.
distractor_notes.C: The admin's home domain is insufficient; global domain is required.
distractor_notes.D: plugin_admin is not a documented role for this requirement; being in the global domain is the requirement.

stem: Where can lesser-used system properties that are not on a standard form be found and edited?

options.text: In the System Dictionary
In the System Property [sys_properties] table
In the System Definition > Scripts module
In the Update Set picker

rationale: Some lesser-used system properties exist only in the System Property [sys_properties] table and are not available on the standard system properties forms. Admins can access and add them directly from this table.

distractor_notes.A: The System Dictionary defines table and field schema, not system properties.
distractor_notes.C: Scripts module is for server-side scripts, not property configuration.
distractor_notes.D: The Update Set picker tracks configuration changes, not property values.

stem: What does the system property 'com.glide.attachment.max_size' control?

options.text: The maximum number of attachments per record
The maximum file attachment size in megabytes
The allowed file extension types for attachments
The maximum total storage for all attachments

rationale: The com.glide.attachment.max_size property sets the maximum file attachment size in megabytes. The default value is 1024 (1GB).

distractor_notes.A: There is no standard property limiting the number of attachments per record.
distractor_notes.C: Allowed file extensions are controlled through a separate security property, not com.glide.attachment.max_size.
distractor_notes.D: This property controls per-file size, not total instance storage.

stem: An admin wants to add a custom module to the Application Navigator for easy access to a frequently used system property list. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Edit the global CSS to add a shortcut link
Add a module in the Application Navigator pointing to the sys_properties table
Create a homepage widget linking to the property list
Use the Admin Center to pin the property

rationale: Administrators can add a module in the application navigator to access the list of system properties. This module provides easy access to add or edit properties in the System Properties table.

distractor_notes.A: CSS modifications are for styling, not application navigator modules.
distractor_notes.C: A homepage widget is a reporting/visualization tool, not the recommended approach for property access.
distractor_notes.D: Admin Center is for application management, not creating custom navigator modules.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a component that an administrator specifies when creating an email notification?

options.text: When to send the notification
Who receives the notification
The physical email server to use
What content is in the notification

rationale: When creating an email notification, administrators specify when to send it, who receives it, what content it contains, and whether it can be delivered as a digest. The physical email server is an instance-level configuration, not part of the individual notification record.

distractor_notes.A: When to send is one of the four key notification components.
distractor_notes.B: Who receives is one of the four key notification components.
distractor_notes.D: Content is one of the four key notification components.

stem: What is an email watermark in ServiceNow notifications?

options.text: A logo image embedded in the email header
A unique label generated at the bottom of each notification email to match incoming email to existing records
A legal disclaimer automatically appended to all outgoing emails
A read-receipt request attached to each notification

rationale: By default, a unique watermark label is generated at the bottom of each notification email. It allows the system to match incoming email replies to the correct existing records.

distractor_notes.A: A watermark is a unique tracking label, not a logo image.
distractor_notes.C: Legal disclaimers are a separate configuration from watermarks.
distractor_notes.D: Watermarks enable record matching, not read receipts.

stem: Can a ServiceNow instance send or receive encrypted email messages?

options.text: Yes, using the Encrypted Email plugin
Yes, if TLS is configured on the mail server
No — the system strips the body of encrypted emails because it cannot process encrypted content
Yes, but only for outgoing emails

rationale: ServiceNow instances cannot send or receive encrypted email messages. The system strips out the body of the encrypted email because it cannot process the encrypted content in plain text or HTML.

distractor_notes.A: There is no Encrypted Email plugin that enables this capability.
distractor_notes.B: TLS encrypts the transport channel but the email body encryption ServiceNow cannot process is end-to-end content encryption.
distractor_notes.D: The limitation applies to both sending and receiving encrypted emails.

stem: What is an email digest in ServiceNow?

options.text: A log of all sent email notifications for a day
A single email that summarizes activity for a notification and its target records during a specified time interval
An archive of all emails older than 30 days
A compressed attachment containing multiple email threads

rationale: An email digest is a single email summarizing activity for a selected notification and its target records during a specified time interval, reducing notification volume when frequent updates occur.

distractor_notes.A: An email digest is not a log; it is a consolidated outgoing summary email.
distractor_notes.C: Email archives are managed through the email retention feature, not digests.
distractor_notes.D: A digest is a consolidated notification email, not a compressed attachment.

stem: What is captured in a standard update set?

options.text: Data records such as incidents and changes
Configuration changes such as form layouts, business rules
User account changes and role assignments
All database transactions since the last commit

rationale: Update sets capture configuration changes — such as form layouts, business rules, client scripts, and UI policies — allowing them to be moved between instances. Data records are not captured.

stem: What state should an update set be in before it can be exported from a source instance?

The update set is exported back to the source instance for review

stem: A developer accidentally leaves the Default update set selected and makes a configuration change. Where will that change be recorded?

The change is recorded in the last used named update set

distractor_notes.D: The change goes to whatever update set is currently selected, which in this case is Default.

options.text: Business rules

Form layouts

admin
security_admin
impersonator

distractor_notes.D: Watermarks are for record matching on inbound emails, not controlling delivery.

stem: A system property does not exist in a base instance. What must an admin do to use it?

sys_group_member

A separately stored SMS template

distractor_notes.B: A write ACL controls editing, not visibility/reading.

stem: What is a Catalog Item in the ServiceNow Service Catalog?

options.text: A business rule that triggers when a user accesses the catalog
A requestable offering that users can order through the Service Catalog
A report showing catalog usage metrics
An ACL rule that restricts catalog access by role

rationale: A Catalog Item is a requestable offering presented to users in the Service Catalog. When a user orders a catalog item, a request and request item are created.

distractor_notes.A: Business rules are server-side automations, not catalog offerings.
distractor_notes.C: Catalog usage metrics are reports, not catalog items.
distractor_notes.D: ACL rules control access; they are not catalog items.

stem: What are catalog variables used for?

options.text: To define which users can view a catalog item
To collect input from the user when they order a catalog item
To set the pricing of catalog items
To schedule when a catalog item becomes available

rationale: Catalog variables are form fields that collect input from users when they are submitting a catalog item request, such as the name of the new hire or the type of equipment needed.

distractor_notes.A: User access to catalog items is controlled by user criteria, not variables.
distractor_notes.C: Pricing in the catalog uses a different pricing mechanism, not variables.
distractor_notes.D: Availability scheduling is separate from variables.

stem: Which catalog item type creates a record in a table other than the default sc_req_item table when submitted?

options.text: Standard catalog item
Record Producer
Order Guide
Content Item

rationale: A Record Producer is a special type of catalog item that creates a record in a specified target table (e.g., Incident or HR Case) when submitted, rather than creating a standard request item.

distractor_notes.A: Standard catalog items create records in sc_req_item.
distractor_notes.C: Order Guides group multiple catalog items into a single request, they do not target a custom table.
distractor_notes.D: Content Items are informational catalog entries, not request-generating items.

stem: What is an Order Guide in the Service Catalog?

options.text: A document explaining how to configure the Service Catalog
A catalog item that groups multiple items for a user to request together in a single order
A workflow that automates fulfillment of catalog requests
A category used to organize catalog items visually

rationale: An Order Guide groups multiple catalog items into a single guided ordering experience, allowing users to request several related items together in one request.

distractor_notes.A: Order Guides are functional catalog constructs, not documentation.
distractor_notes.C: Fulfillment workflows are separate from order guides.
distractor_notes.D: Categories organize items visually; order guides group items for ordering.

stem: What is a Scheduled Job (Scheduled Script Execution) in ServiceNow?

options.text: A client-side script that runs when a user logs in
A server-side script configured to run automatically at specified time intervals
A notification triggered by a calendar event
A flow that activates on a record insert

rationale: A Scheduled Job is a server-side script configured to run automatically at defined time intervals (e.g., daily, hourly, weekly). They are stored in the sys_trigger table.

distractor_notes.A: Client-side scripts run in the browser; scheduled jobs are server-side.
distractor_notes.C: Scheduled jobs are not calendar notifications; they execute scripts automatically.
distractor_notes.D: Flows triggered on record insert are Flow Designer triggers, not scheduled jobs.

stem: Which table stores Scheduled Job records in ServiceNow?

options.text: sys_job
sys_schedule
sys_trigger
sys_event

rationale: Scheduled Job records (Scheduled Script Executions) are stored in the sys_trigger table in ServiceNow.

distractor_notes.A: sys_job is not the standard table for scheduled jobs.
distractor_notes.B: sys_schedule is used for schedules (work hours definitions), not scheduled jobs.
distractor_notes.D: sys_event stores platform events, not scheduled jobs.

stem: Where does an administrator change the company logo displayed in the Next Experience top bar?

options.text: System Properties > CSS
System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16
System Definition > Tables
User Preferences > Theme

rationale: The company logo shown in the Next Experience top bar is configured in System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16, which includes banner/branding settings.

distractor_notes.A: System Properties > CSS controls custom styling, not the logo upload.
distractor_notes.C: System Definition > Tables is for data model management, not branding.
distractor_notes.D: User Preferences > Theme lets individual users change their theme, not the instance-wide company logo.

stem: Which Business Rule timing is used to set display-only values visible to the user on a form, without modifying the database record?

options.text: Before
After
Display
Async

rationale: A Display Business Rule runs when a record is loaded into a form and can set display-only (g_scratchpad) values that are visible to the user without modifying the actual database record.

distractor_notes.A: Before rules run before the DB write; they modify actual record values.
distractor_notes.B: After rules run after the DB write; they are not for display-only values.
distractor_notes.D: Async rules run after commit in a background thread, not for display value computation.

stem: Which Client Script type runs when a user edits a cell value directly in a list view?

options.text: onLoad
onChange
onSubmit
onCellEdit

rationale: An onCellEdit Client Script runs when a user edits a cell value directly in a list, as opposed to editing on a form. This is specific to inline list editing.

distractor_notes.A: onLoad runs when a form is loaded, not during list cell edits.
distractor_notes.B: onChange runs on form fields, not list cell edits specifically.
distractor_notes.C: onSubmit runs when a form is saved, not during list cell edits.

stem: An admin creates a UI Policy that makes the Resolution Notes field mandatory when State is 'Resolved'. What must they also configure to ensure the field is no longer mandatory when State changes away from Resolved?

options.text: Create a second UI Policy for all other states
Enable the 'Reverse if false' option on the UI Policy
Add an onLoad Client Script to reset mandatory flags
Set the field mandatory flag to false in the dictionary

rationale: The 'Reverse if false' option automatically removes the mandatory attribute from Resolution Notes when the condition (State = Resolved) is no longer true, without needing a second UI Policy.

distractor_notes.A: A second UI Policy is unnecessary when Reverse if false handles the reversal automatically.
distractor_notes.C: An onLoad Client Script could achieve this but is more complex and not the intended approach for UI Policies.
distractor_notes.D: Setting mandatory in the dictionary makes it always mandatory, which is the opposite of what is needed.

stem: In a ServiceNow ACL, what does it mean when the 'Role' field is left empty?

options.text: The ACL is disabled and does not apply
Any authenticated user can perform the operation
Only the admin role can perform the operation
The ACL applies only to guest (unauthenticated) users

rationale: When the Role field in an ACL rule is left empty, any authenticated user can perform the protected operation, regardless of their roles, as long as any script conditions also pass.

distractor_notes.A: An empty role means open access, not disabled.
distractor_notes.C: Admin-only access requires explicitly specifying the admin role.
distractor_notes.D: Guest user access is controlled separately; an empty role applies to authenticated users.

stem: A 'Before' Business Rule sets current.priority = 1 on an incident. When is this value written to the database?

options.text: Immediately when the script executes
At the end of the Before rule execution, before the DB insert/update
After all After rules have also run
Only if the user saves the form manually again

rationale: In a Before Business Rule, changes to current fields (like current.priority = 1) are applied to the record object and then written to the database as part of the pending insert/update that happens at the end of the Before phase.

distractor_notes.A: The value is queued to be written as part of the database operation, not immediately in isolation.
distractor_notes.C: After rules run after the DB write; the Before rule's changes are already committed by then.
distractor_notes.D: The user does not need to save again; the Before rule's changes are included in the current save operation.

stem: What is an email layout in the context of ServiceNow notifications?

options.text: The CSS stylesheet applied to all instance pages
Reusable content for the message body of email templates
The page structure definition for Service Portal
A responsive dashboard layout for email clients

rationale: Email layouts provide reusable content for the message body of email templates, allowing admins to create consistent HTML structures that can be applied across multiple templates.

distractor_notes.A: CSS stylesheets control instance page appearance, not email notification layouts.
distractor_notes.C: Service Portal page structure uses separate layout components, not email layouts.
distractor_notes.D: Email layouts are for notification templates, not dashboards.

stem: A scoped application defines a role with the 'Elevated privilege' flag set. What is the significance of this flag?

options.text: The role is automatically assigned to all admin users
The role can only be used in production instances
Users must explicitly elevate to this role during a session to use it, even if it is assigned to them
The role grants access to all tables in global scope

rationale: Roles with the 'Elevated privilege' flag require users to explicitly request elevation to that role within their session, adding a layer of security for sensitive operations. Simply being assigned the role is not enough — elevation is required each session.

distractor_notes.A: Elevated privilege roles are not auto-assigned to admins.
distractor_notes.B: Elevated privilege is a session security feature, not an environment restriction.
distractor_notes.D: The role's elevated privilege flag does not automatically grant access to all global tables.

stem: An admin needs to run a GlideRecord cleanup script every night at midnight. What is the correct tool to use?

options.text: A Flow Designer scheduled trigger
A Business Rule with Async timing
A Scheduled Job (Scheduled Script Execution)
An onLoad Client Script with a time check

rationale: A Scheduled Job (Scheduled Script Execution) is designed exactly for running server-side scripts on a defined time schedule such as nightly at midnight.

distractor_notes.A: Flow Designer scheduled triggers can also work but Scheduled Jobs are the traditional and direct tool for time-based GlideRecord scripts.
distractor_notes.B: Async Business Rules trigger on database operations, not on a clock schedule.
distractor_notes.D: Client Scripts run in the browser and cannot execute timed server-side cleanup scripts.

stem: What does a 'table' type ACL with operation 'read' protect?

options.text: Whether a specific field value can be read
Whether a user can see ANY records from that table
Whether a user can run a specific UI action
Whether a user can see the table in the system dictionary

rationale: A table-level read ACL determines whether a user can see any records from that table at all. If a user fails the table-level read ACL, they cannot see any records even if they would pass row-level checks.

distractor_notes.A: Field-value read access is controlled by field-level ACLs, not table-level ACLs.
distractor_notes.C: UI action access is controlled by UI Action conditions, not table read ACLs.
distractor_notes.D: System dictionary visibility is an admin-level concern, not governed by table read ACLs for end users.

stem: Which Update Set state indicates that changes have been successfully applied to the target instance?

options.text: Complete
Loaded
Previewed
Committed

rationale: After running commit on a target instance, the update set enters the Committed state, indicating all configuration changes have been successfully applied.

distractor_notes.A: Complete is set on the source instance before export, not the target after applying.
distractor_notes.B: Loaded means the update set has been imported but not yet previewed or committed.
distractor_notes.C: Previewed means the system has checked for collisions but has not yet applied the changes.

stem: Which table stores Requested Item records created when a catalog item is ordered?

options.text: sc_catalog
sc_request
sc_req_item
sc_cat_item

rationale: When a user orders a catalog item, a Requested Item record is created in the sc_req_item table. The sc_request table holds the parent request record.

distractor_notes.A: sc_catalog stores catalog definitions, not ordered items.
distractor_notes.B: sc_request holds the parent request, not the individual line item.
distractor_notes.D: sc_cat_item stores the catalog item definitions (the offerings), not the orders.

stem: A Business Rule updates related change records when an Incident priority changes to 1. During testing, the developer notices the rule fires even when the priority does not change. What condition should they add?

options.text: current.active == true
current.priority.changesTo(1)
previous.priority != 1
current.priority == 1 && previous.priority != current.priority

rationale: Using current.priority.changesTo(1) in the Business Rule condition ensures it only fires when the priority field changes TO the value 1, preventing unnecessary executions when the record is updated for other reasons.

distractor_notes.A: Checking active status does not prevent the rule from firing on unchanged priority updates.
distractor_notes.C: previous.priority != 1 would fire when priority was not previously 1, which could include updates where priority didn't change.
distractor_notes.D: This condition works logically but current.priority.changesTo(1) is the cleaner and more idiomatic ServiceNow approach.

stem: Which two elements in an ACL rule must BOTH evaluate to true for access to be granted?

options.text: The user must have the specified role
The user must be in the global domain
Any script condition must return true
The record must be in an active state

rationale: For an ACL rule to grant access, the user must have the required role (if specified) AND any script condition defined on the ACL must return true. Both conditions must be satisfied.

distractor_notes.B: Domain membership is not a universal ACL requirement unless domain separation is configured.
distractor_notes.D: Record active state is not a built-in ACL evaluation criterion.

stem: What is the purpose of User Criteria on a catalog item?

options.text: To collect input from users ordering the item
To control which users can see or order the catalog item
To define approval workflows for the item
To set pricing rules for different user groups

rationale: User Criteria on a catalog item defines which users can see or order the item, based on conditions such as role, department, location, or company. This replaces the older role-based catalog visibility approach.

distractor_notes.A: Collecting user input is the purpose of catalog variables, not user criteria.
distractor_notes.C: Approval workflows are defined in the catalog item's workflow/flow, not user criteria.
distractor_notes.D: Pricing rules are a separate catalog configuration, not user criteria.

stem: What is the purpose of the 'itil' role in ServiceNow?

options.text: Grants full administrative access to all platform settings
Grants access to ITSM process modules such as Incident, Problem, and Change
Grants read-only access to all tables
Grants access to the Service Catalog only

rationale: The itil role grants users access to ITSM process modules including Incident, Problem, Change, and related applications. It is the standard role for service desk agents and ITSM practitioners.

distractor_notes.A: Full admin access is granted by the admin role, not itil.
distractor_notes.C: Read-only access to all tables is not what itil provides; it grants ITSM operational access.
distractor_notes.D: Service Catalog access is controlled by user criteria, not specifically by the itil role.

stem: What does the 'Notification Categories' feature allow admins to do?

options.text: Group and identify related notifications in user notification settings
Set priority levels for notification delivery
Archive notifications after a defined period
Restrict notifications to specific user groups

rationale: Notification categories let admins create groupings that identify related notifications in user notification settings, making it easier for users to manage their subscription preferences.

distractor_notes.B: Notification priority/delivery order is not set through categories.
distractor_notes.C: Archival is handled by email retention, not notification categories.
distractor_notes.D: Restricting notifications to user groups is done through the notification's Who receives settings, not categories.

stem: Where does a Business Rule execute compared to a Client Script?

options.text: Business Rules run in the browser; Client Scripts run on the server
Both run on the server
Business Rules run on the server
Both run in the browser

rationale: Business Rules are server-side scripts that execute on the ServiceNow server. Client Scripts are client-side scripts that execute in the user's browser.

distractor_notes.A: This is backwards — Business Rules are server-side, Client Scripts are client-side.
distractor_notes.B: Client Scripts specifically run in the browser, not the server.
distractor_notes.D: Business Rules specifically run on the server, not the browser.

stem: What is the significance of the 'Retrieve Update Sets' step on a target instance?

options.text: It pushes update sets from source to target via the network
It pulls update sets from a remote source instance into the current target instance
It validates that all update sets are collision-free before import
It creates a backup of the current target configuration

rationale: The Retrieve Update Sets step allows a target instance to pull update sets directly from a connected source instance over the network, rather than requiring a manual XML export and import.

distractor_notes.A: The target pulls, the source does not push — the direction is pull from target.
distractor_notes.C: Validation happens during Preview, which is a separate step after retrieval.
distractor_notes.D: No backup is created during the retrieve step.

stem: An admin needs to display a custom base URL in all outbound email notifications instead of the default instance URL. Which system property should they set?

options.text: glide.email.from.address
glide.email.override.url
glide.email.base_url
glide.system.url

rationale: The glide.email.override.url property is used to display a custom base URL in email notifications instead of the default instance URL.

distractor_notes.A: glide.email.from.address controls the sender email address, not the base URL.
distractor_notes.C: glide.email.base_url is not a documented standard property for this purpose.
distractor_notes.D: glide.system.url is not the documented property for overriding email notification URLs.

stem: Which table stores the catalog item definitions (the offerings available to users)?

options.text: sc_request
sc_req_item
sc_cat_item
sc_catalog

rationale: Catalog item definitions — the offerings shown to users in the Service Catalog — are stored in the sc_cat_item table.

distractor_notes.A: sc_request stores the parent request record when a user places an order.
distractor_notes.B: sc_req_item stores the request item (ordered instance) records.
distractor_notes.D: sc_catalog stores the catalog containers/groupings, not individual item definitions.

stem: Which Business Rule condition method checks if a field value has changed from any previous value to a specific new value?

options.text: current.field.changed()
current.field.changesTo(value)
current.field.changesFrom(value)
previous.field != current.field

rationale: current.field.changesTo(value) returns true when the field's value has changed to the specified value during this update. It checks both that the field changed AND that the new value equals the specified value.

distractor_notes.A: current.field.changed() returns true if the field changed to any value, not a specific one.
distractor_notes.C: current.field.changesFrom(value) checks if the field changed FROM a specific previous value, not TO one.
distractor_notes.D: previous.field != current.field checks if the value changed at all, not if it changed to a specific value.

stem: A developer needs to make the Resolution Code field visible only when an incident's State is set to 'Resolved' via a client-side mechanism. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: An onChange Client Script that checks State and shows/hides the field
A UI Policy with condition State = Resolved and the Visible action on Resolution Code
A Business Rule that sets the field's mandatory flag
An ACL that hides the field for non-Resolved states

rationale: A UI Policy is the recommended no-code/low-code approach for showing or hiding fields based on field conditions. It handles the toggle automatically including the Reverse if false behavior.

distractor_notes.A: An onChange Client Script can work but requires scripting; UI Policy is the recommended declarative approach.
distractor_notes.C: Business Rules are server-side and cannot control UI field visibility in real-time.
distractor_notes.D: ACLs control access based on roles, not real-time form state conditions.

stem: An admin needs to audit which users have a specific role, including those who inherited it through group membership. Where should they look?

options.text: The sys_user table, filtering by role field
The Roles related list on the role record
The sys_user_has_role table, filtering by role sys_id
The audit log for recent role assignment changes

rationale: The Roles related list on a role record shows all users who have that role, including those who have it directly and those who inherited it through group membership.

distractor_notes.A: The sys_user table does not have a direct 'role' field that lists all assigned roles.
distractor_notes.C: sys_user_has_role is not the standard table name for this query; sys_user_role is the junction table.
distractor_notes.D: The audit log shows changes, not a current list of all users with a role.

stem: Before building a configuration change in a sub-production instance, an admin wants those changes captured so they can be moved to production later. What should they do first?

options.text: Create and select an update set as the current update set
Switch the application scope to Global
Activate a plugin
Impersonate an admin

rationale: Set a current update set before making changes — captured configuration is recorded into the active set so it can be moved later. If you build first with Default selected, those changes aren't grouped for transport.

distractor_notes.B: Scope affects where artifacts live, not whether changes are captured for transport.
distractor_notes.C: Activating a plugin adds features; it doesn't capture your changes.
distractor_notes.D: Impersonation tests another user's experience; it doesn't record changes.

references.title: Create and select an update set as the current set

stem: An admin finished changes in a development instance and wants to move that update set to production. What is the correct order of operations?

options.text: Mark Complete in dev, then retrieve, preview, and commit in production
Commit it in dev, then it auto-appears in production
Export each record manually to production
Delete it in dev so production regenerates it

rationale: The lifecycle is: mark the set Complete in the source, then in the target retrieve it, Preview (to catch collisions), and Commit. Preview before commit is the safety step that surfaces conflicts before they land.

distractor_notes.B: Committing in dev applies it there; it doesn't transport to production automatically.
distractor_notes.C: Manual record export defeats the purpose of update sets and is error-prone.
distractor_notes.D: Deleting a set doesn't regenerate anything in production.

stem: During Preview of a retrieved update set, the system reports collisions. What does this mean and what should you do?

options.text: Incoming changes conflict with local changes
The update set is empty and can be ignored
Commit anyway — collisions resolve themselves automatically
The instance must be reinstalled

rationale: Collisions flag where the incoming update set conflicts with changes already on the target. Preview lets you review and resolve (accept/skip) each one before committing, so you don't overwrite something important by accident.

distractor_notes.B: Collisions mean there ARE changes that conflict — not that the set is empty.
distractor_notes.C: Committing without resolving can overwrite or break things; resolve first.
distractor_notes.D: Reinstalling is unnecessary and unrelated to update set collisions.

stem: A new team of 12 agents all need the same set of roles, and membership will change over time. What is the most maintainable way to grant access?

options.text: Assign the roles to a group and add the users to the group
Assign each role to each user individually
Give the team the admin role
Share one login among the team

rationale: Granting roles to a group and managing membership means access updates automatically as people join or leave — far easier than per-user role grants. It's the standard, maintainable access pattern.

distractor_notes.B: Per-user grants multiply maintenance and drift as the team changes.
distractor_notes.C: Admin is a massive over-grant and a security risk.
distractor_notes.D: Shared logins break accountability and violate security practice.

references.title: Assign a role to a group

stem: An admin wants to verify what a specific end user can see and do after an access change, without logging out. What's the safe way to check?

options.text: Impersonate the user
Reset the user's password and log in as them
Grant themselves the user's manager role
Edit the user's session record

rationale: Impersonation lets an admin temporarily experience the platform exactly as that user — same roles and ACL outcomes — to confirm access is correct, then switch back. It's logged and far safer than borrowing credentials.

distractor_notes.B: Logging in as someone via a password reset is insecure and unnecessary.
distractor_notes.C: Adding roles to yourself changes your own access, not a test of theirs.
distractor_notes.D: Editing session records isn't a supported way to test access.

stem: While building in a scoped application, an admin finds they can't directly modify a record that belongs to the Global scope. Why?

options.text: Application scope protects artifacts
Their account lacks the itil role
The instance is in maintenance mode
Scoped apps cannot contain any records

rationale: Application scope isolates and protects each app's artifacts. Editing across scopes is restricted by default (and governed by the target app's settings), which prevents one app from accidentally changing another's components.

distractor_notes.B: This is a scope boundary, not an itil-role issue.
distractor_notes.C: Maintenance mode blocks logins generally, not specific cross-scope edits.
distractor_notes.D: Scoped apps absolutely contain records; they're just protected by scope.

stem: An admin wants to try a plugin's features safely before using it in production. What is the recommended practice?

options.text: Activate it on a sub-production
Activate it directly in production during business hours
Edit the plugin's source files manually
Add it to an update set instead of activating it

rationale: Plugins should be activated and evaluated in a sub-production instance first, often with the optional demo data, so you can validate behavior before touching production. Some plugins can't be deactivated cleanly, which makes testing first important.

distractor_notes.B: Activating untested in production risks disruption during business hours.
distractor_notes.C: You don't hand-edit plugin source; you activate it.
distractor_notes.D: Plugin activation isn't captured by update sets the way configuration is.

stem: Stakeholders should get an email when an incident's Priority becomes 1. Which configuration delivers this?

options.text: An email notification triggered by the record condition
A UI policy on the incident form
A favorite
A coalesce field

rationale: Email notifications send messages when their trigger conditions are met — here, when Priority becomes 1 — to the recipients you define. UI policies and favorites don't send email.

distractor_notes.B: UI policies change form behavior; they don't send notifications.
distractor_notes.C: Favorites are personal shortcuts, not alerts.
distractor_notes.D: Coalesce is an import-matching concept.

stem: An admin needs to change an instance-wide behavior controlled by a system property but isn't sure of the exact name. Where can they look them up?

options.text: The system properties (sys_properties) list of available properties
The user's watch list
The incident form layout
A transform map

rationale: System properties (sys_properties) hold instance-wide configuration values; you can browse the available properties to find and adjust the right one. Changing the wrong property can have broad effects, so confirm before editing.

distractor_notes.B: Watch lists handle notifications, not configuration values.
distractor_notes.C: Form layout controls one form's fields, not instance-wide settings.
distractor_notes.D: Transform maps handle imports, not system properties.

stem: An organization wants its own logo to appear in the instance header. Which administrative option changes this?

options.text: The instance banner/logo branding setting
A business rule on sys_user
An ACL on the logo field
A scheduled job

rationale: Branding settings let an admin replace the header logo (and related visual elements) with the organization's own. It's a configuration setting, not something you script.

distractor_notes.B: Business rules run record logic; they don't set the header logo.
distractor_notes.C: ACLs control access, not branding.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduled jobs run on timers, unrelated to branding.

references.title: Change instance banner logo in Next Experience

stem: Which TWO are true about moving configuration with update sets?

options.text: You should Preview a retrieved set before committing it
The set should be marked Complete in the source before transport
Update sets capture data records like incidents and users
Committing in the source instance moves it to the target automatically

rationale: Two safe-transport truths: mark the set Complete in the source before moving it, and Preview in the target before Commit to catch collisions. Update sets carry configuration, not operational data, and committing in the source doesn't transport anything.

distractor_notes.C: Update sets capture configuration changes, not data records like incidents or users.
distractor_notes.D: Committing applies the set where you commit; transport requires retrieving it in the target.

stem: Which TWO statements about roles and groups are correct?

options.text: Roles can be granted to users directly or through groups
A role can contain other roles
Only the admin can ever hold more than one role
Granting a group a role removes it from all individual users

rationale: Roles are flexible: assign them directly or via group membership, and a role can contain other roles that come along when granted. Users can hold many roles, and group grants add access rather than stripping it from individuals.

distractor_notes.C: Any user can hold multiple roles — that's normal.
distractor_notes.D: Group role grants are additive; they don't remove users' existing roles.

references.title: Assign a role to a user

stem: A teammate reports their configuration changes can't be moved to test because everything went into the Default update set. What practice would have prevented this?

options.text: Create and select a named update set before making changes
Make changes in the Default set, then rename it later
Edit records directly in the test instance instead
Export each changed record by hand

rationale: Changes captured in the Default set aren't meant to be transported. Selecting a named update set before working ensures the changes are grouped and movable. It's the core update-set discipline.

distractor_notes.B: The Default set isn't designed for transport; renaming after the fact isn't the supported flow.
distractor_notes.C: Editing directly in test skips change control and won't promote consistently.
distractor_notes.D: Hand-exporting records is error-prone and defeats update sets.

references.title: Create and select an update set as the current set

stem: An email notification should go to the incident's Assigned to and its Watch list. How are recipients like these specified on a notification?

options.text: Use the 'Who will receive' options
Hard-code every email address in the body
Add recipients with a coalesce field
Set recipients in a UI policy

rationale: Notifications define recipients through the 'Who will receive' settings — specific users/groups, the user in a field (like Assigned to), and options such as the record's watch list. That keeps recipients dynamic per record.

distractor_notes.B: Hard-coding addresses can't follow the record's actual assignee or watchers.
distractor_notes.C: Coalesce is an import-matching concept.
distractor_notes.D: UI policies change form behavior, not notification recipients.

stem: Several notifications should share the same branded greeting and footer. What lets you reuse that content instead of retyping it in each notification?

options.text: An email template
A coalesce field
A watch list
A dictionary override

rationale: Email templates store reusable message content (and can include field variables), so multiple notifications share consistent, branded text without duplication.

distractor_notes.B: Coalesce matches import records.
distractor_notes.C: Watch lists define recipients, not reusable content.
distractor_notes.D: Dictionary overrides change field behavior on extended tables.

stem: With high security settings enabled, an admin tries to modify an ACL and is blocked until they elevate privileges. Which role must they elevate to?

options.text: security_admin (elevated privilege)
itil
approver_user
catalog_admin

rationale: Editing access controls under high security requires elevating to the security_admin role for the session — an extra safeguard so ACL changes are deliberate. The other roles don't grant ACL editing.

distractor_notes.B: itil supports ITSM work, not ACL administration.
distractor_notes.C: approver_user handles approvals.
distractor_notes.D: catalog_admin manages the service catalog, not ACLs.

stem: A team wants a custom application whose tables and artifacts are isolated and protected from accidental changes by other apps. Which model should they use?

options.text: A scoped application
The Global scope
A single business rule
An update set

rationale: Scoped applications namespace and protect their own artifacts, with controlled boundaries for cross-scope access. Global is the legacy shared space without that isolation.

distractor_notes.B: Global lacks the isolation/protection that scoping provides.
distractor_notes.C: A business rule is logic, not an application container.
distractor_notes.D: Update sets move configuration; they don't define app isolation.

stem: An admin wants to toggle a platform behavior on or off instance-wide. Which type of system property value is appropriate?

options.text: A true/false (boolean) property
A reference to a user
A coalesce field
A watch list

rationale: System properties come in types including true/false, string, and integer. A boolean property is the right choice for an on/off, instance-wide toggle.

distractor_notes.B: A user reference points to a person, not an on/off setting.
distractor_notes.C: Coalesce is an import concept.
distractor_notes.D: Watch lists define notification recipients.

stem: Security asks which users currently hold the admin role. What's the most direct way to answer?

options.text: Query the user role assignments
Read the update set log
Check each user's favorites
Open the import set table

rationale: Role grants are stored as user-to-role records (sys_user_has_role). Filtering that for the admin role lists exactly who holds it — the standard way to audit role membership.

distractor_notes.B: Update set logs track configuration moves, not role membership.
distractor_notes.C: Favorites are personal shortcuts.
distractor_notes.D: Import set tables stage incoming data.

stem: After committing an update set in test, a problem surfaces and the team wants to reverse those changes. What capability supports this?

options.text: Back out the committed update set
Delete the instance database
Re-import the data via a transform map
Add the change to a watch list

rationale: A committed update set can be backed out, reversing the captured changes it applied. It's the controlled way to undo a problematic promotion rather than scrambling to fix things manually.

distractor_notes.B: Dropping the database is catastrophic and unnecessary.
distractor_notes.C: Transform maps move data, not undo configuration changes.
distractor_notes.D: Watch lists send notifications; they don't revert changes.

stem: An admin wants new functionality that ServiceNow ships but which isn't active yet on the instance. What action turns it on?

options.text: Activate the relevant plugin
Create a business rule
Add a coalesce field
Personalize the form

rationale: Plugins package optional features; activating the plugin makes its capabilities available. Best practice is to try it in a sub-production instance first.

distractor_notes.B: Business rules add logic but don't enable shipped feature sets.
distractor_notes.C: Coalesce is an import concept.
distractor_notes.D: Form personalization changes a view, not platform features.

stem: Why is impersonation preferred over creating a test account to verify a user's experience?

options.text: It reproduces the actual user's roles and is logged, with an easy switch back
It permanently grants you their roles
It disables ACLs while active
It edits the user's stored password

rationale: Impersonation runs as the real user — their exact roles and ACL outcomes — and is logged for accountability, with a quick return to your own session. A separate test account may not match the real user's access.

distractor_notes.B: Impersonation is temporary; it doesn't permanently grant roles.
distractor_notes.C: ACLs still apply — that's the point of testing access accurately.
distractor_notes.D: It doesn't touch the user's password.

stem: Which TWO are update-set best practices?

options.text: Use a named update set rather than Default for changes you intend to move
Preview a retrieved set and resolve collisions before committing
Commit in the source instance to transport it to the target
Store imported incident data in the update set

rationale: Use a named set (not Default) and preview/resolve collisions before commit — two pillars of safe promotion. Committing in the source doesn't transport it, and update sets carry configuration, not operational data.

distractor_notes.C: Committing applies the set where you commit; transport requires retrieving it in the target.
distractor_notes.D: Update sets capture configuration, not data records like incidents.

stem: Which TWO are true about email notifications?

options.text: They can be triggered by record conditions or events
Recipients can be derived from record fields like Assigned to or the watch list
They require a coalesce field to send
They can only be sent to a single hard-coded address

rationale: Notifications fire on conditions/events and can target dynamic recipients pulled from record fields (Assigned to, watch list, and more). No coalesce is involved, and recipients aren't limited to one hard-coded address.

distractor_notes.C: Coalesce is an import-matching concept, unrelated to notifications.
distractor_notes.D: Recipients can be multiple and dynamic, not a single fixed address.
